answer: The crystal multiplier is published, charged in copper, and raven lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2111 identities would post 1994 proofs and burn roughly 29 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
